IM10-01.why: All four are plausible small sums; 30/15/10 all divide 180 and 11 is prime-shaped, but nothing makes any value illegal as a sum of distinct primes.

IM10-02.why: 66 is the count of ALL vertex pairs (sides included) and 108 is the uncorrected double count; 54 is exactly half of 108, and a diagonal count must be the halved, side-subtracted member of that family.

IM10-03.why: 650000 is the odd one out by form - the only non-power-of-ten, built by adding the mantissas - but the three remaining powers of ten are indistinguishable without multiplying.

IM10-04.why: The option set is exactly the category column of the table, so every option is a legal mode value; nothing narrows it.

IM10-05.why: 35 is a bare echo of the given percent and answers the wrong unit; item IM10-22 supplies the correspondence 126 degrees = 7/20 = 35% of a circle, which fixes 126 as the degree value of a 35% sector.

IM10-06.why: 108 is the raw un-converted product of the two givens and 36 is one division by 3; the stem says the linear conversion applies twice, so the key is two steps down the /3 chain, and 16 is off that chain entirely.

IM10-07.why: 2200, 2420, 2662 form a x1.1 chain, so they are the year-1, year-2 and year-3 balances; the stem asks for year 2, which makes 2200 and 2662 answers to different questions.

IM10-08.why: 314 is a proper part of the requested TOTAL (the lateral piece) so it cannot be the total, and 471 is the sum-shaped option that 785 is built from (785 = 314 + 471).

IM10-09.why: 2 is the untransformed sum of P's own coordinates, an echo of the given point; the reflection sends the larger-magnitude coordinate negative, so a positive 12 is not reachable.

IM10-10.why: A perfectly symmetric set of one magnitude and its reciprocal in both signs carries no information at all with the computation withheld.

IM10-11.why: 2 is a bare restatement of the midpoint's x-coordinate, which is a given rather than a derived sum; the other three are all legal coordinate sums.

IM10-12.why: 1130.4 is exactly 3 x 376.8, i.e. the cylinder value, and the stem quotes the 1/3 factor, so the key is the small member of that x3 pair; 1507.2 is 4 x 376.8, off the formula.

IM10-13.why: Every option is a simple combination of the stem's 2, 5 and 11 (5, 5/2, 11+5, (11+5)/2), so no option can be argued illegal from the set.

IM10-14.why: 14 and 15 are the adjacent off-by-one pair that a 'least integer' stem always brackets the boundary with; 28 and 11 sit far off that boundary - but the set does not say which side of the strict inequality wins.

IM10-15.why: 150 is one eighth-part and 450 is exactly 3 x 150, matching the stem's '3 out of every 8'; 400 is the town total split in thirds, a ratio the stem never states.

IM10-16.why: Four distinct weekdays, none of them the stated starting day; the option set constrains nothing.

IM10-17.why: 21 is a raw given; 15 and 24 are the before and after ranges and so answer 'what is the range', not 'by how much does it increase'; only 9, the difference of those two, has the shape the stem asks for.

IM10-18.why: 2 is an echo of the worked example's leaf and is far too small to be a nine-score range spanning three stems, as is 9; between 15 and 21 the three-stem span favours the larger.

IM10-19.why: The ratio has 12 parts over 180 degrees, so every angle is a multiple of 15 - that rejects 126 and 84 - and of the two survivors only the larger can be 7 of 12 parts.

IM10-20.why: The set encodes its own givens: 11/24 carries numerator 3+8 and denominator 3x8, while 1/24 is the product rather than the sum and 1/11 is its inverted shard.

IM10-21.why: 26 and 16 are just the two givens doubled, an echo family; a number-line distance between a negative and a positive point is the sum of the magnitudes, which is the option-shape 21 has.

IM10-22.why: 1/3 of a circle is 120 degrees, contradicting the stem's stated 126, and 2/5 is the 144-degree sector, i.e. a different question; 7/20 and 7/40 share the numerator but only one keeps the sectors summing to a whole.

IM10-23.why: 8 is the stem's own stated prior median, an unchanged-value echo; a six-element median is an average of two middles, and 10 is the option that is the mean of two other options (8 and 12).

IM10-24.why: 121 is the given area restated, 11 is the side (a sub-answer, not a perimeter) and 22 is half the perimeter; only 44 is 4 x the side that the option set itself supplies.

IM10-25.why: 16 is the odd one out by magnitude, clearly off the 34/36/38 cluster; within that cluster the options are deliberately adjacent and carry no distinguishing structure.

IM10-26.why: 17 and 18 are echoes of the square root of the upper bound rather than counts; 11 and 12 are the genuine off-by-one count pair and the set gives no way to pick between them.

IM10-27.why: 450, 530 and 730 are all consecutive-year differences while 820 spans two years, answering a different question; of the legal consecutive differences the stem asks for the greatest.

IM10-28.why: The stem pins a multiple of both 4 and 6, and 100 and 102 each fail one of those, leaving 108 and 120 - of which the stem asks for the least.

IM10-29.why: 25 is the given restated in the wrong unit and 12.5 is that given halved; a clock face turns 6 degrees per minute, so only an option that scales the minutes UP can be a degree measure.

IM10-30.why: 12.5 is the odd one out by form (the only decimal, and just half the hypotenuse); the option set plus the givens 25 and 7 completes a recognised integer triple at 24, with 20 belonging to the 15-20-25 triple the stem does not supply.
